# Reading the build-241 cache (test build)

The server can now run on the vanilla OSRS build-241 cache (OpenRS2 cache 2746) instead of GadScape's own
rev-211 cache. GadScape's custom items, maps and interfaces are not in that cache, so this is a test build.

## Running

```
-Dgadscape.cache.dir=/path/to/cache241     # main_file_cache.dat2 + idx0..24 + idx255
```

* `CacheManager.loadCacheFiles` opens that directory (read-only) instead of `cache/data/cache/`
  (GameLoader is unchanged; the property wins over the path it passes).
* The definition format (211 or 241) is chosen per cache by `CacheFormat.detect`: a cache with archive 24
  (gamevals), or archive 22 with sized reference tables, is 241. `-Dgadscape.cache.revision=211|241` overrides it.
* Nothing repacks the external cache: `TypeParser.main` returns at once, `:app:generateCache` and
  `:app:generateCacheProd` are skipped, and `XTEALoader.load` does nothing (241 maps have no XTEA keys).
* `./gradlew :app:runDev -Dgadscape.cache.dir=...` passes every `-Dgadscape.*` property to the server JVM.
* `-Dgadscape.cache.strict=true` turns unknown opcodes and half-read definitions into exceptions (used by the
  verifiers below). Without it, each unknown opcode is logged once per type and decoding carries on as before.

## What changed

### jagcached (`mgi.tools.jagcached`)
* `Archive`: reference-table flags 0x4 (compressed + uncompressed size per group) and 0x8 (CRC of the
  uncompressed group) are read in the client's order (ids, names, crcs, uncompressed crcs, digests, sizes,
  versions, file counts, file ids, file names) and written back by `pack()`; a protocol-7 table stays protocol 7.
  Every archive of build 241 is protocol 7 with flag 0x4 (archives 6, 8, 10, 12, 13 also have names).
* `Group` keeps those values and recomputes them when it is repacked.
* `ArchiveType`: `ANIMAYAS(22)` and `GAMEVALS(24)`. Build 241 has no archive 16 or 23: `Cache` opens a missing
  idx file as an empty `Index`, `Cache.hasArchive` says whether an archive exists, and the 255/255 descriptor
  writes crc 0 / version 0 / empty digest for it.
* The master index accepts groups up to 16 MiB (the 241 models reference table is 525,411 bytes; the old limit was
  500,000), regular indexes too (was 1,000,000).
* `Helper.crc32` no longer shares one `CRC32` between threads.
* `JS5Responses` serves every archive the cache has (still skipping 16), not just the `ArchiveType` entries.
  (The NET track serves JS5 through rsprot; this keeps the old path correct.)

### Config decoders
All ported from RuneLite master (330e650, BSD-2; licence text kept in the ported files), checked against it value
by value (see Verification). Opcodes marked 241 are new; nothing changed for rev 211 except where noted.

| Type | Changes |
|---|---|
| item | 44-54: 4-byte model ids (inventory, male/female 0-2, heads); 15 tradeable=false; 160 stackable=2 (on charged/untradeable items such as Abyssal tentacle, not "stackable" for `isStackable()`); 161 holding whitelist; 200-202 ground sub-ops/conditional ops; 251 flag |
| npc | 61/62: 4-byte models/chathead models; 42 full recolour; 111 = render priority 2 from rev 233 (rev 211 keeps "follower"); 122 follower; 123; 126 footprint; 129, 130, 145, 147 flags; 146 overlap tint; 251-253 ops |
| object | 6/7: 4-byte models; 42; 78/79 retain byte for all 241 objects (211 keeps the old id <= 47337 rule); 90, 91, 93, 94, 95, 96; 100-102 ops; 249 params are now kept |
| sequence | rev 226 layout: 13 skeletal id, 14 sounds by frame with a weight byte, 15 keyframe range, 16 vertical offset, 17 masks, 18 debug name, 19 flag |
| spotanim | 3: 4-byte model; 9 debug name; 10 not clickable; 42 |
| param | 7 default long; 8 type by var-type id |
| enum | 7 long values, 8 default long (long enums are kept but not registered as Int/String enums) |
| struct, inventory | params of type 2 (long); inventory 249 params |
| identkit | 5: 4-byte models; 65-69 and 70-79 chathead models |
| dbrow/dbtable | cells read by base type: string (36), long (35, 49, 56, 71, 110, 115, 116), else int. RuneLite reads longs as ints; no 241 column uses a long type, so both agree |
| hitbar | sprite ids read as the client's nullable big smart (32767 = -1) |
| map element | opcode 16 (no payload) |
| interface | rev 237: type-6 model ids are 4-byte ints (IF1 and IF3) |
| clientscript | rev 237: 16-byte trailer with long local/argument counts; LCONST (61) has an 8-byte operand, PUSH_NULL (63) a 1-byte one; scripts too short for a trailer (241 script 0 is `00 0a`) decode as empty |

Other behaviour changes:
* `AnimationDefinitions.getDuration()` returns (end - start) * 20 ms for skeletal sequences (it returned 0). Many
  241 sequences are skeletal, so death/attack delays would otherwise be 0.
* `ByteBuffer.readParameters` reads type 2 as a long.

### Maps
* `MapFiles` finds a square's terrain and locs in either layout: rev 211 named groups (`m{x}_{y}`, `l{x}_{y}` with
  XTEA) or rev 237+ groups keyed by region id with no names and no XTEA.
* Files of a 241 map group (RuneLite RegionLoader, OpenRune GameMapDecoder and zwyz's osrs-cache unpacker agree):
  0 = terrain ("m"), 1 = locs ("l"), 2 = environment ("e": lighting/fog/sky), 3 = "t", 4 = "w" (none of the three
  reference decoders reads 3 or 4). The server needs only 0 and 1. Group 25287 (square 98,199) is not a map square
  but world-area definitions; `MapFiles` skips it.
* Tile and loc encodings are unchanged, but build 241 appends one flags byte to the terrain; bit 0 means a fifth
  "underwater" level follows (only square 64,73 has one). The server builds collision from levels 0-3 as before;
  locs on level 4 are skipped (Region already did; DynamicRegion now does too instead of wrapping to level 0).
* Switched to `MapFiles`: `Region.loadRegionMap` (now `loadRegionMapOrThrow` + a wrapper that logs the cause),
  `DynamicRegion`, `AreaType` (existence check without decompressing), `WorldMapUtils` (its clip-settings reader
  also read attributes as bytes, a pre-209 leftover), `Regions.inject`.
* Still by name and rev 211 only (cache tools, not run by the server): `TypeParser`, `DataMigration`, `MapPacker`,
  `EdgevilleRestore`, the finder tools.

## Verification

```
# 1. every archive, config, interface, clientscript and map, plus a value-by-value comparison with RuneLite master
server/cache/scripts/build-runelite-reference.sh <runelite checkout> <lombok-1.18.38.jar> <out dir>   # prints the jar list
./gradlew :cache:verifyCache --offline -Dgadscape.cache.dir=<cache241> -Dgadscape.rlref.jar=<printed list>

# 2. collision for every map square through Region/RegionMap
./gradlew :core:verifyRegions --offline -Dgadscape.cache.dir=<cache241>

# both tasks write their classpath, so they can be re-run without Gradle, e.g. the rev-211 regression run:
java -Xmx3g -cp "$(cat cache/build/verify-cache-classpath.txt)" -Dgadscape.cache.dir=<vanilla 211 cache> \
    com.gadscape.cache.verify.CacheVerifier
```

Results on the build-241 cache (OpenRS2 2746), 2026-10-21:

* Reference tables: 23 archives present (16 and 23 missing), 120,049 groups; for every group the stored CRC,
  the compressed size and the uncompressed size (flag 0x4) match the data. All archives are protocol 7.
* The server's runtime loaders (all 21 `Definitions` classes, as GameLoader/Main call them) load in strict mode.
* Every config file decodes in strict mode, 0 failures: 34,732 items, 16,772 NPCs, 63,256 objects,
  15,156 sequences, 4,444 spotanims, 5,961 enums (3,349 of them only the end opcode), 4,045 structs, 2,774 params,
  19,631 varbits, 1,032 inventories, 307 identkits, 659 overlays, 256 underlays, 90 hitbars, 1,269 map elements,
  271 dbtables, 17,063 dbrows.
* 980 interfaces with 26,834 components (2,096 IF1, 24,738 IF3, 5,338 model components); 10,187 clientscripts
  (44 use longs).
* 2,949 map squares, 5,020,905 locs, every terrain and loc file read to the last byte.
* RuneLite master comparison: 247,766,218 values compared, 0 mismatches, and every config, interface, script and
  map file is byte-identical between jagcached and RuneLite's own reader.
* Collision (`:core:verifyRegions`): 2,949 squares, 0 failures; 44,990,464 tiles, 4,181,641 with a blocked floor,
  2,739,478 object-blocked, 943,170 with walls; all 2,024,405 blocking type-10/11 locs have the OBJECT flag on
  their tile (47,198 more sit on level 0 under a bridge and are dropped, as the client does); the Lumbridge spawn
  tile (3222, 3218, 0) is walkable.
* Regression on the vanilla 211 cache (same verifier, no RuneLite comparison because RuneLite's defaults are the
  newest formats): every archive and config decodes in strict mode (27,831 items, 12,141 NPCs, 47,337 objects,
  10,045 sequences, 23,044 components, 7,033 scripts, 2,118 terrains); loc groups need XTEA keys, which are not
  available here.

Accepted quirks (the decoders read exactly what the client reads, these leave bytes the client also ignores):
* 4 IF3 model components of 241 (19:19, 272:4, 415:70, 428:4) have exactly one of widthMode/heightMode set; the
  cache holds both obj width and height, the client reads one, 2 bytes stay unread.
* Vanilla 211 sequence 8127 has 291 frames and stores the sound count as a byte (35); the client reads 35 sounds,
  768 bytes stay unread.
* 241 clientscript 0 is two bytes (`00 0a`), too short for a trailer; RuneLite cannot read it either.

## Id constants whose meaning changed (211 -> 241)

No item, NPC or object id was deleted, so `ItemId`, `NpcId` and `ObjectId` are left as they are. Comparing the
cache names of every constant between vanilla 211 and 241 (ignoring case/punctuation and ids that were "null" in
211): NpcId 192 renamed (16 used in code), ItemId 137 (44 used), ObjectId 851 (53 used). The full list, used or
not, is in `rev241-renamed-ids.txt`.

Most important: several NPCs the server spawns became transforming "null" NPCs in 241 and the real NPC moved to a
new id, so spawning the old id shows something else:

| Constant | 211 | 241 at that id | new 241 ids of the old NPC |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NpcId.TURAEL` 401 | Turael | null, varbit 451 -> Light creature | 13433, 13434, 13560, 13618 |
| `NpcId.MAZCHNA` 402 | Mazchna | null, varbit 10839 -> Thaerisk | 13438-13440, 13561, 13620 |
| `NpcId.DURADEL` 405 | Duradel | null, varbit 10839 -> Thaerisk | 13441, 13562, 13622 |
| `NpcId.GHOMMAL` 2457 | Ghommal | null, varbit 10839 | 13437, 13556, 13613 |
| `NpcId.HARRALLAK_MENAROUS` 2458 | Harrallak Menarous | null, varbit 10929 | 13430-13432, 13557, 13615 |
| `NpcId.SLOANE` 2473 | Sloane | null, varbit 10780 | 13447, 13558, 13616 |
| `NpcId.KEY_MASTER` 5870 | Key Master | Patchy | 12599 |
| `NpcId.MAC` 6481 | Mac | Jack Frost | 1053 |
| `NpcId.CAPTAIN_TOBIAS` 3644, `SEAMAN_LORRIS` 3645, `SEAMAN_THRESNOR` 3646, `CUSTOMS_OFFICER` 3648 | Port Sarim crew | null, varbit 18314 -> same name at 14978-14985 (Sailing) | |
| `NpcId.VYRE_ORATOR` 8323 | Vyre Orator | null, varbit 15464 -> 16281 | 16281, 16282 |
| `NpcId.RANTZ` 1470 | Rantz | null, varp 293 -> 14793/14794 | 4855-4857, 14793, 14794 |

slayer masters and Warriors' Guild NPCs turn into unrelated NPCs, so their spawns need the new ids. Every renamed

## Approximated or missing
* Rev 241 definitions are decoded to keep every definition aligned; most new fields (sub-ops, conditional ops,
  sound weights, environment...) are read and dropped because the server has no use for them yet.
* Frame sounds: a 241 frame can carry several sounds (72 frames do); `AnimationDefinitions` keeps the last.
* Underwater (level 4) terrain and locs, and map files 2-4, are not used by the server.
* Encoders (`encode()`/`pack()`) still write the rev-211 formats (2-byte model ids etc.): packing GadScape content
  into a 241 cache is a later step.
* The cache tools that build GadScape's own cache (TypeParser, DataMigration, custom packers) are rev 211 only.
